decisive_items: Laryngoscopy revealed thickening of the epiglottic mucosa with irregularity and white plaques
Laryngeal biopsy revealed rare hyphae and yeast forms on Grocott methenamine silver stain
Fungal culture grew Histoplasma capsulatum, identified by typical tuberculate microconidia
response.rationale: The vignette localizes the infection to the larynx with biopsy and culture confirming Histoplasma capsulatum, making laryngeal histoplasmosis the most specific and accurate diagnosis. R4 is broader and lacks anatomical specificity.

rejected.why: ICL is the underlying immunodeficiency, not the active diagnosis.
Immunodeficiency-related histoplasmosis is less specific than laryngeal histoplasmosis and does not capture the localized presentation.
Candida was cultured but biopsy and culture confirmed Histoplasma, not candidiasis.
Histoplasmosis is correct but lacks the laryngeal localization supported by laryngoscopy and biopsy.
Disseminated histoplasmosis is not supported; no systemic symptoms and only subtle lung opacities, while laryngeal findings dominate.
